छत्तीसगढ़ में इंटर्न डॉक्टरों का प्रदर्शन (photo source- Patrika)
Chhattisgarh Intern Doctors Protest: छत्तीसगढ़ के शासकीय चिकित्सा महाविद्यालयों में एमबीबीएस 2021 बैच के इंटर्न डॉक्टरों ने स्टाइपेंड बढ़ाने की मांग को लेकर प्रदेशव्यापी सांकेतिक प्रदर्शन किया। शुक्रवार को सभी सरकारी मेडिकल कॉलेजों में इंटर्न डॉक्टरों ने शांतिपूर्ण तरीके से अपनी मांगों को लेकर आवाज उठाई। इसी क्रम में शासकीय चिकित्सा महाविद्यालय (GMC) राजनांदगांव में शाम 5 बजे अस्पताल परिसर में प्रदर्शन आयोजित किया गया। इसमें करीब 200 से 250 इंटर्न डॉक्टर, मेडिकल विद्यार्थी, पीजी रेजिडेंट और यूजी बॉन्डेड डॉक्टर शामिल हुए।
प्रदर्शन कर रहे इंटर्न डॉक्टरों ने वर्तमान में मिल रहे 15 हजार 900 रुपए प्रतिमाह स्टाइपेंड को बढ़ाकर 30 हजार रुपए प्रतिमाह करने की मांग की है। डॉक्टरों का कहना है कि पिछले तीन वर्षों से स्टाइपेंड में कोई बढ़ोतरी नहीं हुई है, जबकि इस दौरान महंगाई, रहने-खाने का खर्च और काम का दबाव लगातार बढ़ा है। इंटर्न डॉक्टरों को अस्पतालों में 24 घंटे मरीजों की देखभाल, इमरजेंसी ड्यूटी, वार्ड प्रबंधन और अन्य महत्वपूर्ण जिम्मेदारियां निभानी पड़ती हैं। उनका कहना है कि इतनी जिम्मेदारियों के बावजूद मिलने वाला मानदेय मौजूदा परिस्थितियों के हिसाब से काफी कम है।
इंटर्न डॉक्टरों के इस आंदोलन को प्रदेश के कई मेडिकल संगठनों का समर्थन मिला है। आईएमए-एमएसएन छत्तीसगढ़, आईएमए-जेडीएन, जेडीए और आरजेडीए समेत कई संगठनों ने स्टाइपेंड बढ़ाने की मांग का समर्थन किया है। आईएमए-एमएसएन छत्तीसगढ़ के प्रदेश अध्यक्ष शाहदिल खुसरू ने कहा कि इंटर्न डॉक्टरों के स्टाइपेंड बढ़ाने का मुद्दा अब तक पांच बार स्वास्थ्य मंत्री के सामने रखा जा चुका है। उन्होंने कहा कि युवा डॉक्टरों की मांगों को लेकर संगठन लगातार समर्थन कर रहे हैं।
इंटर्न डॉक्टरों ने सरकार को सोमवार तक मांगों पर निर्णय लेने का समय दिया है। उन्होंने चेतावनी दी है कि यदि इस अवधि तक कोई सकारात्मक फैसला नहीं लिया गया तो आंदोलन के अगले चरण में ओपीडी और अन्य गैर-आपातकालीन सेवाओं का बहिष्कार किया जाएगा। हालांकि प्रदर्शनकारियों ने स्पष्ट किया है कि मरीजों की परेशानी को देखते हुए आपातकालीन सेवाएं जारी रहेंगी।
इंटर्न डॉक्टरों ने कहा कि उनका आंदोलन किसी सेवा को बाधित करने के लिए नहीं, बल्कि अपने अधिकारों और सम्मानजनक स्टाइपेंड की मांग को लेकर है। उन्होंने सरकार से जल्द निर्णय लेकर इंटर्न डॉक्टरों की समस्याओं का समाधान करने की अपील की है। प्रदेशभर में हुए इस प्रदर्शन के बाद अब स्वास्थ्य विभाग के अगले कदम पर सभी की नजरें टिकी हैं।

Skip to contentBlistering heat likely this weekend and early next week
GRAND JUNCTION, Colo. (KKCO) - This weekend will be hot with triple digits in the Grand Valley and mid-to-upper 90s elsewhere.
A Heat Advisory is in effect from noon Sunday until 9 AM Monday for the Grand Valley including areas around Grand Junction, Fruita, Clifton, Palisade, Orchard Mesa, the Redlands, and surrounding areas. Temperatures of 101 to 105 degrees are expected in the Grand Valley on Sunday and Monday. Humidity is easing, but it will still be high enough to add to the heat stress and increase the risk of heat stroke or heat exhaustion. If you have to be outside, don’t overdo it. Make sure you’re drinking plenty of water and eating well, and stay in the shade as much as you can. Inside in the air conditioned is by far the better option. Know the symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke, and call 911 in the event of heat stroke.
Remember your pets need extra water and a cool place out of the sun, too. Asphalt can be hotter than 140 degrees when air temperatures are 95 degrees. Paw burns can happen in minutes. Shaded grass is the best area to walk your pets to keep them safe. The temperature inside your car can be as high as 119 degrees in 10 minutes when the outside air temperature is 100 degrees. In just 30 minutes, the inside of your vehicles can be hotter than 130 degrees. Never leave people or pets inside of vehicles, even with the windows down. The heat is deadly.
Saturday will be sunny and hot. We’ll warm from upper 60s and lower 70s at 7 AM to low-to-mid 90s at noon, then to high 90s and lower 100s at 4 PM. High temperatures in the afternoon will be near 102 degrees around Grand Junction, 98 degrees around Montrose, 102 degrees around Delta, 98 degrees around Cortez, and 106 degrees around Moab. Low temperatures in the morning will be near 70 degrees around Grand Junction, 62 degrees around Montrose, 64 degrees around Delta, 61 degrees around Cortez, and 72 degrees around Moab.
Highs in the 90s and 100s are likely to persist through next week. The peak heat will happen on Sunday and Monday, then we’ll simmer through Friday. Some limited cooling can happen next week. We will still be hot, but we should be able to come down out of the 100s.

Saturday, August 01
Mangalore Today News Network
In Dakshina Kannada, widespread rainfall was recorded in Mangaluru, Puttur, Uppinangady, Karaya, Kalleri, Madanthyaru, Guruvayanakere, Dharmasthala, Kokkada, Venur, Nelyadi, Kadaba, Sullia, Subrahmanya, Bellare, Panja, Kalmakaru, Moodbidri, Mulki, Panambur, Ullal, Bajpe, Vitla, Kanyana and Peruvai. Several low-lying areas in Mangaluru city experienced waterlogging following continuous showers.
In view of the prevailing weather conditions, the Dakshina Kannada Deputy Commissioner urged parents to ensure that children stay away from waterlogged areas, lakes, riverbanks and seashores. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea.
District and taluk-level officials have been directed to remain at their headquarters to ensure effective disaster management. They have also been instructed to respond promptly to public complaints, maintain constant contact with the District Control Room and keep relief centres ready in every taluk.
Residents requiring emergency assistance related to natural disasters can contact the District Control Room by dialling 1077 or 0824-2442590.
Meanwhile, Udupi district also witnessed widespread rainfall accompanied by strong winds. Trees were uprooted at several places, resulting in damage to houses.
A tree fell on a house in the DCM Colony of Kasturba Ward in Udupi city, causing partial damage. While intermittent rain was reported during the morning, some areas experienced brief sunny spells in the afternoon before heavy showers returned later in the day.
Light to moderate rainfall was recorded across Udupi, Manipal, Kundapura, Byndoor, Hebri, Karkala, Kapu and Brahmavar taluks, with rural areas receiving heavier showers during the evening. Rising water levels in rivers, streams and canals, along with waterlogging on several roads, caused inconvenience to motorists.
The IMD has issued an Orange Alert for both Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts for August 1, forecasting heavy rainfall accompanied by strong winds. Wind speeds of up to 60 kmph are expected along the coast, and fishermen have once again been advised not to venture into the sea. Authorities have also urged the public to remain vigilant and take necessary precautions.

45 mm Rain Overnight, Ahmedabad Wakes Up To Flooded Roads And Red Alert
Ahmedabad witnessed another spell of heavy rainfall late Friday night, bringing 45 mm of rain and pushing the city into a red alert for Saturday. While Friday daytime remained relatively dry, the overnight downpour led to severe waterlogging across several parts of the city, disrupting traffic, affecting public transport, and leaving many commuters stranded.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned that more heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over the next 24 hours, asking residents to remain cautious and avoid unnecessary travel.
Overnight Rain Brings Relief From Heat but Creates New Problems
After a largely dry Friday, rain returned with intensity during the night. According to the IMD, Ahmedabad received 45 mm of rainfall, enough to flood low-lying roads and cause traffic congestion across many parts of the city.
The sudden spell brought down temperatures and provided relief from the humid weather. However, the heavy rain also exposed the city’s drainage issues, with several roads submerged under rainwater within a short period.
Officials said the city had been under an orange alert on Friday, but the forecast was upgraded to a red alert on Saturday due to the possibility of more intense rainfall.
Western Parts of Ahmedabad Worst Affected
The western parts of Ahmedabad were among the worst-hit areas, where roads turned into waterlogged stretches, making it difficult for vehicles to move.
Commuters travelling during the morning hours faced long delays as traffic moved slowly through flooded roads. Many two-wheelers stalled in the water, while buses and cars struggled to pass through submerged streets.
Public transport services were also affected, forcing passengers to wait longer or look for alternative travel options.
Rainfall Recorded Across the City
Rainfall was recorded in several parts of Ahmedabad, with different areas receiving varying amounts of rain.
Among the major locations:
Fatewadi recorded the highest rainfall at around 63 mm. Bodakdev received around 47 mm. Bopal recorded 40 mm. Science City received around 34.5 mm. Usmanpura recorded approximately 33.5 mm. Aasarwa received around 32.5 mm. Paldi recorded nearly 31.5 mm. Chandkheda received around 30 mm.
The widespread rainfall ensured that almost every part of the city experienced moderate to heavy showers.
AMC Activates Flood Response Measures
Following the heavy rainfall forecast, the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) activated its flood response system.
The civic body placed flood-control teams on alert and deployed emergency personnel across vulnerable locations. Officials also kept pumping stations, drainage teams, rescue staff, and engineering personnel on standby to respond quickly if the rainfall intensified.
Control rooms continued monitoring the situation throughout the night, while civic teams remained ready to clear blocked drains and remove accumulated rainwater wherever required.
IMD Predicts More Heavy Rainfall Today
The IMD has forecast that Ahmedabad is likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall on Saturday as a strong weather system continues to influence Gujarat.
The forecast also indicates that several districts across Gujarat may receive widespread rainfall, with isolated places expected to witness extremely heavy showers.
Residents have been advised to remain indoors during periods of intense rain, avoid travelling through waterlogged roads, and stay away from rivers, lakes, and underpasses that may flood quickly.
Authorities Urge Citizens to Stay Alert
Authorities have appealed to citizens to remain cautious, especially those living in low-lying areas. Motorists have been advised to drive carefully as visibility may reduce during heavy showers and several roads could remain submerged.
Emergency teams remain on standby, and the administration is closely monitoring the weather situation as Ahmedabad prepares for another day of intense monsoon activity.
With the city now under a red alert, officials expect the next few hours to be crucial, urging residents to follow weather advisories and avoid unnecessary movement until conditions improve.
